description:
Found by s507d checking what -E enables.  perl 5.40.3 vs pcl on main 50dbd195:
  printf "use feature ':5.40';\ntry { die \"x\\\\n\" } catch (\$e) { print \"caught \$e\" }\n" > t2.pl
  perl t2.pl -> caught x
  pcl  t2.pl -> PCL: statement dropped at t2.pl line 2: try ... -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case ...
                then dies "PCL: statement not supported at t2.pl line 2"
The same with `pcl -E 'try {...} catch ($e) {...}'`, because -E IS `use feature ':5.40'; use builtin ':5.40';` in front of the program (PCLSwitches::_prefix).
Works: `use v5.40;` before the try, `use feature 'try';`, and `pcl -E 'use feature "try"; try ...'` on one line.
Likely the PPI feature-include callback (the #360 family) recognises the bundle of `use v5.NN` but not the `:5.NN` bundle names of `use feature`.  The fix belongs to that callback in Pl/, not to -E.  docs/pcl-commands.md notes the workaround under -E until it is fixed.


=== DONE (s507c, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) ===
MEASURED: perl 5.40.3's %feature::feature_bundle -- try is in 5.39/5.40/all, signatures in 5.35+/all, neither in default.  Pl::Parser::_pcl_feature_include_cb answered `use v5.NN` and the feature NAMES, and returned {} for a `:5.40` argument (so PPI's own logic was skipped and nothing was enabled).
FIX (in the ONE callback): a bundle name `:5.NN` (a third component ignored), `:all`, `:default` ADDS (with `no`, removes) the features the same thresholds give `use v5.NN`, without resetting the rest; a bare `no feature` resets both to off.  The string-eval inheritance (#364) follows for free (presumed_features).
PROBES (scratch/s507c/m2/t01-t12, perl -> base -> tree): :5.40, :all, :5.40.1, :5.39 + try (base: DROP + die); :5.36 (holds signatures, not try: try stays a sub -- breaking case, same on base); no feature ':5.40' and bare no feature after use feature 'try' (base: "Parser2 TODO: try without a catch"); :5.40 inside a block (try outside stays a sub); eval q{try…} inherits the bundle; :default; :all signatures; :5.40 + finally.  All 12 = perl on the tree; `pcl -E 'try {…} catch ($e) {…}'` prints caught x.
GUARDS: Pl/t/feature-pragma-01.t 33 -> 43 rows (6 callback rows + 2 end-to-end + 1 eval row fail on the base; the :default row and the block row's outer half are breaking cases); Pl/t/pcl-switches-01.t row "-E: try/catch is on" (fails on the base).  docs/pcl-commands.md: the -E row's "For now try/catch also needs use feature 'try'" sentence removed, try/catch listed.
subject: `try`/`catch` is not recognised under `use feature ':5.40'` (a feature BUNDLE), so `pcl -E 'try { die "x\n" } catch ($e) { print "caught $e" }'` drops the statement and dies "statement not supported" (perl: caught x); `use v5.40` and `use feature 'try'` work (found by s507d, main 50dbd195)
